before: Checking and translating source into a form that can become an executable.
after: Checking source code and turning it into a form used to build a runnable program.

before: A conversion that can lose information, rejected in this brace-initialization example.
after: A conversion that could lose information, such as putting a fractional value into a whole-number type.

before: A single-quoted C++ character value, distinct from a double-quoted string literal.
after: A value written in single quotes, such as the ordinary letter 'A'. Double-quoted text is a different kind of value.

before: An object whose value cannot be modified through its const declaration.
after: An object whose value cannot be replaced through its const name.

before: Reading a formatted value from an input stream while tracking success or failure.
after: Trying to read a value from an input stream and checking whether that read succeeded.

before: A labeled branch selected from an integral or enum value.
after: A label that chooses where a switch starts when its value matches.

before: A loop that advances a counter while its condition permits.
after: A loop that updates a counter and keeps going while its test is true.

before: A C++ standard-library sequence that can resize and owns its element storage.
after: A sequence that owns its items and can grow or shrink.

before: A typed standard container with a fixed number of elements.
after: A sequence that owns a fixed number of items of one chosen type.

before: A C++ loop that visits elements supplied by a range.
after: A loop that visits each item in a sequence.

before: Another name bound to an existing C++ object.
after: Another name for an object that already exists.

before: A parameter that borrows an object without permitting changes through that reference.
after: A function input that refers to the original object but does not allow changes through that reference.

before: A pointer used to observe an object whose lifetime is controlled elsewhere.
after: A pointer that can reach an object but does not take responsibility for keeping it alive or destroying it.

before: The period during which an object exists and can be validly accessed.
after: The time during which an object exists.

before: A function sharing a name with another function but having a different input signature.
after: One of several functions with the same name but different parameter lists.

before: A distinct enum type whose named values are qualified with the enum name.
after: A type with named choices written under that type, such as State::Ready.

before: A rule an object preserves across its public operations.
after: A rule an object must keep whenever its public operations finish.

before: Constructor syntax that initializes a member before the constructor body runs.
after: The constructor part that gives a member its starting value before the constructor body runs.

before: Tie a resource to an owning object whose destruction releases it.
after: Put a resource in an owner that releases it when the owner is destroyed. Resources include memory and open files.

before: A distinct object initialized from another object; member types determine how copying behaves.
after: A separate object initialized from another. Its members decide what the copy shares or duplicates.

before: Operations may transfer resources from a source that remains valid under its documented postconditions.
after: Let an operation transfer owned resources. What remains in the source depends on that type's promises.

before: Prefer member types that already manage ownership so no custom special member functions are necessary.
after: Use members that already handle copying, moving, and cleanup so your class needs no custom functions just to repeat that work.

before: A move-only owning pointer with exactly one owner of its resource.
after: A pointer that owns an object by itself and handles cleanup. It can move but cannot be copied.

before: A non-owning observer of shared ownership that can request a temporary owner with lock().
after: An observer that does not keep an object alive. lock() tries to obtain a temporary shared owner.

before: Choose an overriding member using the actual object type through a base reference or pointer.
after: Choose a virtual function using the actual object behind a base pointer or reference.

before: A base destructor enabling derived cleanup during polymorphic deletion.
after: A destructor that lets deletion through a base pointer start with the actual derived object's cleanup.

before: A family of functions generated for supplied or deduced template arguments.
after: A function pattern that the compiler uses to make functions for chosen types or other template inputs.

before: A family of class types parameterized by types or other template arguments.
after: A class pattern that makes distinct types from chosen types or other template inputs.

before: A named compile-time requirement used to constrain template arguments.
after: A named requirement that template inputs must meet before the program can run.

before: A lambda’s selected surrounding values or references, with different mutation and lifetime effects.
after: The way a lambda uses nearby local values, either by keeping copies or by referring to the originals.

before: A wrapper holding a compatible copyable callable behind a declared call signature.
after: A wrapper that can store different copyable function-like objects with matching input and result types.

before: A range containing its first position but excluding its ending position.
after: A range that includes its starting position and stops before its ending position.

before: The end position returned by a search to represent no matching element.
after: The ending position used by a search result to mean that no matching item was found.

before: A consistent strict comparison relation required by ordering algorithms.
after: A consistent rule for what comes first: nothing comes before itself, order stays consistent through chains, and ties form consistent groups.

before: An iterable description that computes or selects elements as it is traversed rather than storing all results.
after: A description of how to select or compute items when visited, without first storing all the results.

before: A container change makes previously obtained positions unusable under the container’s rules.
after: A change that makes saved iterators no longer valid to use as before.

before: A collection that locates stored values through keys rather than sequence positions.
after: A collection that finds values through keys rather than numbered sequence positions.

before: Locating a key using a hash to select candidate storage, followed by equality checking.
after: Use a hash number to choose where to look, then compare keys to find a match.

before: A set keeps at most one key from each comparator-equivalent group.
after: A set keeps one key from each group treated as equal by its comparison rule. For ordinary integers, repeated equal numbers count once.

before: A value wrapper that distinguishes a contained T from an empty state.
after: A wrapper containing either a value or nothing. A contained zero is different from nothing.

before: One of the explicitly listed types that a variant may currently hold.
after: One of the allowed types that a variant can hold at a time.

before: A typed success-or-error return value whose caller can inspect either state.
after: A returned value that holds either success data or an error, with the caller checking which arrived.

before: A place that catches a failure and decides whether and how the application can continue.
after: A place where the program catches a failure and decides how to continue.

before: On failure, the operation preserves the original observable protected state.
after: If an operation fails, the state it promises to protect stays as it was before the attempt.

before: Simplifying a path’s components without resolving actual filesystem objects.
after: Simplify a path's spelling without checking what exists on disk or following filesystem links.

before: A file-opening mode that directs writes to the end rather than replacing the existing contents.
after: Write at the end of a file while keeping its existing contents.

before: A borrowed character range whose lifetime does not extend that of the underlying storage.
after: A starting position and length for borrowed text. It does not own or keep the original storage alive.

before: A non-owning view of a contiguous sequence, carrying its element type and length.
after: A borrowed view of items stored next to one another, together with their count.

before: An expression that satisfies the language rules for evaluation in a constant-evaluation context.
after: A calculation or value that meets the rules for evaluation before the program runs.

before: Preprocessor conditions that keep a header’s contents from being included twice in one translation unit.
after: Preprocessor checks that prevent a header's contents from appearing twice while one source file and its includes are processed.

before: A source file together with the text produced by preprocessing its includes and directives.
after: One source file together with its included text after preprocessor directives have been handled.

before: A compiler message that explains a detected problem or suspicious construct.
after: A compiler message about a detected error or possible problem.

before: A condition checked during execution when assertions are enabled; failure terminates this simple test program.
after: A check made while a program runs. When enabled, a false assert reports a failure and aborts the program.

before: A count of ticks with an explicit period, such as milliseconds or seconds.
after: An amount of time stored as a count together with a unit, such as milliseconds.

before: A rule mapping an engine’s outputs into values with a specified distribution and range.
after: A rule that turns a random engine's results into values with the requested range and chances.

before: A thread-management lifetime that waits for a joinable worker before the owning scope is left.
after: An owning scope waits for its worker thread to finish before continuing beyond that scope.

before: An indivisible operation that reads a value, computes an update, and writes it as one atomic action.
after: One indivisible operation that reads a value, updates it, and stores the result.

before: An object through which a caller can wait for and retrieve one asynchronous value or exception.
after: An object used to wait for and retrieve a later value or an exception.

before: An explicit rule that maps a current state and input to a next state.
after: A rule that takes the current state and an input, then produces the next state.
